title: ML anomaly detector for proration split anomalies before billing export
creator: Ava Chen
description: Build a machine-learning based anomaly detector that runs as a pre-export validation step for Stripe/NetSuite billing exports. The detector will flag suspicious proration splits, coupon allocations, and fractional rounding cases that historically cause invoice corrections and customer tickets. This ticket covers feature engineering, model training, integration into the export pipeline as a shadow/alert-only check, and a human-in-the-loop triage workflow before any automated remediation. The goal is to catch edge cases that deterministic rules miss and reduce post-export invoice adjustments.
acceptance_criteria: A model that scores each export line-set with an anomaly probability and top-3 contributing features
Shadow runs for 2 weeks over staging exports without modifying production invoices
Detections surfaced in a triage UI (internal) with links to the export batch, affected customer, and historical similar cases
Precision >= 70% at operating point where recall >= 50% on a held-out labeled test set of historical billing corrections
Reduce the ratio of exported batches that later require manual correction by >= 40% in the first 30 days after rollout to alert-only mode
Clear rollback plan and opt-out flag for accounts with high false positive sensitivity
implementation_notes: Pipeline placement: run as last preflight step in the export worker; output anomaly metadata to export manifest and to Sentry/triage dashboard
Model: start with gradient-boosted trees (XGBoost/LightGBM) for tabular features; consider transition to a simple neural model if needed

Features: per-batch aggregates (currency mismatch ratios, coupon presence, sum of fractional cents, number of negative lines, distinct plan versions, mid-period plan swap indicator, late-usage flag, rate-limit-credit flags, hour-of-day skew), sequence features (ordering instability score), and historical account-level drift metrics
Labels: derive positive labels from historical post-export corrections and accounting support tickets (tags: invoice_adjustment, proration_fix, duplicate_line, negative_line_fix)
Model explainability: return SHAP-style top contributors to aid triage and potential auto-fix rules
Alerting thresholds to be initially conservative (high precision), allow manual triage + annotation to expand training set
Export API changes: add optional field anomaly_metadata in export manifest as JSON string (schema documented in Confluence link below)
data_and_datasets: Label sources: accounting corrections table (acct_corrections), support ticket tags, reconciler-run diffs
Priority subset: all chargeable mid-cycle swaps, coupon apportionment events, and burst-credit adjustments from 2024-2026
Holdout set: random 20% of labeled events plus dedicated recent-month time-slice for temporal validation
Synthetic augmentation: inject small fractional rounding perturbations and duplicate-line permutations to increase sensitivity to permutation invariance
evaluation_metrics: Reduction in manual corrections per 10k exports (operational metric)
Time-to-triage: median time for an engineer to inspect flagged batch (target < 30 minutes)
False positive rate against a random sample of non-corrected exports (target < 3%)
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Week 1): Train initial model and run locally against historical exports. Validate metrics and sanity-check SHAP outputs.
Phase 1 (Week 2): Shadow-run in staging export pipeline. Surface alerts only to triage UI and Slack channel #billing-proration-alerts; no export blocks.
Phase 2 (Week 4): Run in production in alert-only mode for selected accounts (5% sample) and collect triage feedback/labels.

Phase 3 (Week 6): Expand to 25% sample; enable suggested auto-fix rules for clear patterns (e.g., tiny cent rounding across many lines) behind a feature flag and require manual approval for account-level changes.
Phase 4 (After success): Consider automatic annotation to downstream reconciler and gradual enablement of non-destructive corrections for low-risk patterns with audit trail and revert capability.
Rollback: export manifest will include anomaly flag; a service flag can disable ML checks per-organization immediately. Documented runbook in Confluence.
